## What is a Bloom filter? {background-image="figures/static/bloom1970.png" background-size="contain" background-position="right" background-opacity="0.5"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Published in 1970 by Burton H. Bloom
- A space-efficient, probabilistic set data structure
- False positives are possible; false negatives are not
- Trades a small error rate for significantly less memory usage
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
- How many people know or have used Bloom filter(s)?
- The original paper: memory was too small for a full hash table, so Bloom traded a small rate of false "yes" answers for a much smaller in-memory structure
  - Illustrative example in the paper (hypothetical, "let us assume"): hyphenating 500,000 words, where 10% need a slow disk lookup. An error-free hash table would need ~2M bits; allowing 1/16 false positives needs <300k bits and still cuts disk reads by 84%
:::
